ground_truth_root_cause: Fastly CDN regional outage in eu-west-1 caused 100% of static asset requests (product thumbnails, etc.) to bypass CDN edge nodes and route directly to the origin asset server. The cart-service origin HTTP connection pool (100 connections max) was rapidly exhausted by the flood of direct origin requests. With the pool saturated, checkout requests that required asset fetches were queued indefinitely, causing p99 latency to exceed 8000ms and an error rate above 34%. This is entirely unrelated to any recent deploy. The logs explicitly show Fastly 503 responses beginning at 13:15:02Z, pool saturation at 13:15:10Z, and a confirmed Fastly statuspage incident notification at 13:15:26Z.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately configure cart-service to skip non-critical asset prefetching during checkout to relieve origin pool pressure. 2. Set a circuit breaker on the CDN fallback path to return placeholder assets instead of hitting origin when CDN fallback rate exceeds 50%. 3. Temporarily increase origin connection pool size from 100 to 500 as a stopgap. 4. Monitor Fastly eu-west-1 statuspage and re-enable CDN routing once Fastly confirms recovery. 5. Post-incident: implement async/lazy asset loading in checkout flow so asset availability is never on the critical path.
red_herring: The promotional discount deploy (SHA e5b7a14d28c41f9b5678efa01123cd45f6a7b8c9, deployed at 10:22Z) is a strong red herring because it (a) modified cart_checkout.js and the pricing engine just 2h53m before the incident, touching the exact code path exercised on POST /cart/checkout which is the failing endpoint, making it natural to suspect the new discount logic introduced a latency regression or blocking computation. However, the logs conclusively exonerate this deploy: at 13:15:13Z and 13:15:30Z debug lines show discount_calc completing in 1ms with correct results even during the outage; at 13:16:01Z the log explicitly states 'No errors in pricing engine; discount_calculator.apply_promotion() completing normally'; and at 13:15:17Z a metrics line confirms discount_calc p99=2ms with no anomaly detected. The actual failure chain begins at 13:15:00Z with the fastly-agent detecting Fastly eu-west-1 degradation, escalates through a cascade of CDN 503 errors forcing origin fallback, and culminates in origin connection pool exhaustion at 13:15:10Z, all of which is entirely independent of any deploy.
